Q: Update Using Case in SQL Server A:

You could make use of a PIVOT with the second table to unify the results to update, as:

update Table1 set
    ColB = T1.ColB_Y,
    ColC = T1.ColC_Y
from Table1 T0
inner join 
(select ColA
    , [2] as ColB_Y
    , [3] as ColC_Y
 from 
    (select * from Table2) X
 pivot (
    max(ColValue)
    for ColB in ([2],[3])
 ) Y) T1 on T1.ColA = T0.ColA

Q: .NET regex to detect missing full stops in thumbnails captions on frwiki A:

This preliminary Find / Replace solution relies mostly on your original regex. A balanced-group section was injected in the caption section as it seems this is the only place needed, but I could be wrong.

The premise here was to use a lookahead to find a valid parameter first. Then it moves past any parameters to get to the Caption ond of those captions, match only the one(s) that do dot have a period anywhere at the end.

Another point of interest is that past the lookahead, when it optionally matches parameters, that itself is entirely enclosed in an atomic. (?> (?:\| parameters)* ) this is necessary so that if a block only contains one parameter, it won't give that back just to satisfy a Caption segment. This is an important necessity.

And some refactor versions below.

Replace with $1$2. to repair.
